source_text: Cum adhuc, inquit, cum prosecutoribus essemus et me pater uerbis auertere et deicere pro sua affectione perseueraret: Pater, inquam, uides, uerbi gratia, uas hoc iacens, urceolum siue aliud? Et dixit: Video. Et ego dixi ei: Numquid alio nomine uocari potest quam quod est? Et ait: Non. Sic et ego aliud me dicere non possum nisi quod sum, Christiana. Tunc pater motus hoc uerbo mittit se in me, ut oculos mihi erueret; sed uexauit tantum, et profectus est uictus cum argumentis diaboli. Tunc paucis diebus quod caruissem patrem, domino gratias egi, et refrigeraui absentia illius. In ipso spatio paucorum dierum baptizati sumus; et mihi spiritus dictauit non aliud petendum ab aqua nisi sufferentiam carnis. Post paucos dies recipimur in carcerem: et expaui, quia numquam experta eram tales tenebras. O diem asperum! Aestus ualidus turbarum beneficio, concussurae militum. Nouissime macerabar sollicitudine infantis ibi. Tunc Tertius et Pomponius, benedicti diaconi qui nobis ministrabant, constituerunt praemio ut paucis horis emissi in meliorem locum carceris refrigeraremus. Tunc exeuntes de carcere uniuersi sibi uacabant: ego infantem lactabam iam inedia defectum; sollicita pro eo adloquebar matrem et confortabam fratrem, commendebam filium; tabescebam ideo quod illos tabescere uideram mei beneficio. Tales sollicitudines multis diebus passa sum, et usurpaui ut mecum infans in carcere maneret; et statim conualuit et releuata sum a labore et sollicitudine infantis, et factus est mihi carcer subito praetorium, ut ibi mallem essem quam alicubi.
thought_title: No Other Name and Prison Turned Bearable
orientation: Perpetua herself now speaks in her prison diary, recording her refusal of her father, her baptism, and her first suffering in prison.
pass_a_gloss: When we were still, she says, with the prosecutors and my father kept on trying with words to turn me aside and to cast me down out of his love: Father, I say, do you see, for example, this vessel lying here, a little pitcher or something else? And he said: I see. And I said to him: Can it be called by another name than what it is? And he says: No. So also I cannot call myself other than what I am, a Christian woman. Then my father, moved by this word, throws himself upon me, so that he might tear out my eyes; but he only harassed me, and he left defeated with the arguments of the devil. Then because for a few days I had been without my father, I gave thanks to the Lord, and I got relief by his absence. In the very space of a few days we were baptized; and the Spirit dictated to me that nothing else was to be sought from the water except endurance of the flesh. After a few days we are received into prison: and I was terrified, because I had never experienced such darkness. O harsh day! Violent heat by reason of the crowd, shakings by the soldiers. At last I was worn down by anxiety for the infant there. Then Tertius and Pomponius, the blessed deacons who were ministering to us, arranged by a bribe that, let out for a few hours, we might get relief in a better place of the prison. Then going out from the prison all were attending to their own business: I was nursing my infant now failing from hunger; anxious for him I was addressing my mother and I was strengthening my brother, I was entrusting my son; I was wasting away because I had seen them wasting away on my account. Such anxieties I suffered for many days, and I claimed it as my right that the infant should remain with me in prison; and at once he recovered and I was relieved from the toil and anxiety for the infant, and the prison suddenly became for me a headquarters, so that I would rather be there than anywhere else.

keeps noun of bearing pain rather than moral patience, and flesh as body under torture
keeps glossary the devil and instrumental sense of sophistries used through the father

pass_b_english: While we were still with the escorts, my father kept at me with his pleas. He loved me, and he tried to turn me from my course and break me down. "Father," I said, "you see that vessel lying there, for example, a little pitcher or something else?" "I see it," he said. "Can it be called by any other name than what it is?" I said to him. "No," he said. "So I also cannot call myself anything other than what I am, a Christian." Roused by that word, my father lunged at me as though to tear out my eyes. He only harassed me, and then he left, defeated along with the arguments of the devil.

When I had been without my father for a few days, I gave thanks to the Lord, and I got relief from his absence. In that span of a few days we were baptized, and the Spirit prompted me to seek nothing from the water except endurance of the flesh. A few days later we were taken into prison. I was terrified, because I had never experienced such darkness. What a harsh day it was! The crowd pressed hard and the heat was fierce, and the soldiers jostled us roughly. In the end I was worn down by worry for my baby there.

Tertius and Pomponius, the blessed deacons who served us, paid a bribe so that we could be let out for a few hours and might get relief in a better part of the prison. Once we had come out of the cell, everyone else attended to their own concerns. I nursed my baby, who was already failing from hunger. Anxious for him, I spoke to my mother, I encouraged my brother, and I entrusted my son. I myself was wasting away, because I saw them wasting away on my account. I suffered such worries for many days, and then I claimed as my right that my baby should stay with me in prison. He grew strong at once, and I was lifted from the strain and worry for my baby. The prison suddenly became a headquarters for me, so that I would rather have been there than anywhere else.
